The haemoglobin level of 11.7 g/dl is more consistent with a primary peritoneal neoplasm, which may cause anemia due to chronic blood loss or nutritional deficiencies, than with a gastrointestinal neoplasm, which may cause anemia due to acute blood loss or iron deficiency.

The normal tumour markers, including carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) and CA125, are more consistent with a primary peritoneal neoplasm, which may not always elevate these markers, than with a gastrointestinal neoplasm, which may elevate these markers, especially CEA.
